slides.title: Interfaces and Pure Virtual Methods
slides.prompt: A pure virtual function (`virtual void fn() = 0;`) has no implementation in base class. A class with at least one pure virtual function is Abstract.

slides.title: Pure Virtual Function Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the syntax initializer to declare a pure virtual function.

slides.title: Abstract Class Instantiation
slides.prompt: What happens if you attempt to instantiate an abstract class directly ('AbstractInterface obj;')?
options: Creates an object with default dummy methods
Instantiates object as a void pointer

slides.title: Concrete Class Requirement
slides.prompt: To instantiate a derived class, it must ___ all inherited pure virtual functions.

slides.title: Pure Virtual Function with Body
slides.prompt: Is it legal in C++ to provide a function body for a pure virtual function?
options: Yes, but it must be defined outside the class body
No, pure virtual functions can never have bodies
Yes, but only if inline inside the class definition
slides.correctAnswer: Yes, but it must be defined outside the class body

slides.title: Interface Idiom in C++
slides.prompt: A C++ class with ONLY pure virtual functions and a virtual destructor is called an ___.
slides.codeSnippet:
// Class acting purely as contract:
Interface

slides.title: Pointers to Abstract Classes
slides.prompt: Can you declare pointers or references of an Abstract Class type?
options: Yes, they are commonly used to point to concrete derived objects
No, abstract class pointers cause compilation errors
Only if the abstract class has no variables
slides.correctAnswer: Yes, they are commonly used to point to concrete derived objects

slides.title: Pure Virtual Destructor Requirement
slides.prompt: If a class declares a pure virtual destructor, it ___ still provide a destructor definition body.
slides.codeSnippet:
// Pure virtual destructor definition body is:
Must

slides.title: Abstract Base Class Pointer Array
slides.prompt: Why are arrays of base abstract class pointers useful in C++?
options: Allows storing heterogeneous concrete derived objects in a unified collection
Reduces total memory used by vector containers
slides.correctAnswer: Allows storing heterogeneous concrete derived objects in a unified collection
